writeup.headline: Oracle rates Sell at 44, one point below Hold, as strong growth meets cash burn and a broken trend.
writeup.thesis: Oracle scores 44, a Sell with Low confidence, sitting just 1 point under the Hold line at 45. Growth is the bright spot at 86, with quarterly revenue up 29.61% year on year and accelerating by 8.98 points, but quality scores only 48 because the FCF margin ex-prepayments is -60.27% (reported -40.0%), and the balance sheet scores 13 with negative free cash flow and cash covering only 0.3 of debt. The trend score is 1: the shares are 58.29% below their 52-week high and 18.83% under the 200-day average, with 12-1 momentum of -53.99%. Valuation scores 41; in absolute terms P/S of 5.5 and EV/EBIT of 20.949 are moderate, while the FCF yield sits 16.168 points below the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history the stock is cheap: P/S is cheaper than at 44 of the last 61 month-ends, EV/EBIT is cheaper than at 58 of the last 61 month-ends, and P/FCF is not comparable (negative now and in 17 of 61 month-ends).
key_risks: Heavy AI data-center spending is driving deeply negative free cash flow; the capex early warning is AMBER at 6/18.
Contract liabilities rose $17.43B, $14.54B more than revenue growth explains, so cash flow leans on customer prepayments.
Backlog may be concentrated in a few AI customers, though this comes from a low-reliability source.
Weak balance sheet: cash covers 0.3 of debt, with negative FCF.
Legal overhang from a pending securities class action and an Oracle Health breach affecting nearly 20M individuals.
what_would_change: A gain of just 1 point, to 45, would lift the rating to Hold, for example from a modest recovery in the trend factor (currently 1).
Free cash flow turning less negative would help both quality and the balance sheet.
Delays at Project Jupiter or a growth slowdown that weakens the growth score of 86 could push the score down; Strong Sell is 15 points away, below 30.
A worsening AI capex warning or adverse news on litigation or customer concentration would add downside pressure.
